newsitem.title: USA: Thrifts back Nationsbank real estate request.
newsitem.headline: Thrifts back Nationsbank real estate request.

text.p: The leading trade group for thrift institutions said it supported NationsBank Corp's application to conduct real estate investing and leasing through a direct subsidiary.

Comptroller of the Currency's Office asked for comments last month on NationsBank's request to conduct real estate activities in a subsidiary rather than through an affiliate of the bank's holding company as currently permitted.
Under a rule adopted by the Comptroller last November, banks may apply for permission to conduct activities that are closely related to banking through direct subsidiaries.

"Federal savings associations have had the ability to engage in real estate finance leasing, either directly or through an operating subsidiary, for some time," the group, America's Community Bankers, said in a letter to the comptroller dated May 5. "Experience has shown that finance leasing can be a safe and sound investment if done prudently."
The NationsBank leasing proposal included adequate safeguards to protect the bank against safety and saoundness risks, the group said.
Thrifts also have experience with real estate development, the group noted.
"Real estate development, such as proposed by NationsBank, can enhance the economic health of the community," the group said.
Such activity should only be permitted in a separate corporate entity and subject to supervisory capital restrictions, the group said.
